facts: A novel statistical singing voice conversion (SVC) technique with direct waveform modification based on the spectrum differential is presented.
The singing voice conversion technique can convert voice timbre of a source singer into that of a target singer.
The singing voice conversion technique does not use a vocoder to generate converted singing voice waveforms.
SVC makes it possible to convert singing voice characteristics of an arbitrary source singer into those of an arbitrary target singer.
Speech quality of the converted singing voice is significantly degraded compared to that of a natural singing voice.
The speech quality degradation is due to various factors, such as analysis and modeling errors in the vocoder-based framework.
A statistical conversion process is proposed to alleviate degradation.
The statistical conversion process directly modifies the signal in the waveform domain.
The statistical conversion process estimates the difference in the spectra of the source and target singers' singing voices.
The differential spectral feature is directly estimated using a differential Gaussian mixture model (GMM).
The differential Gaussian mixture model (GMM) is analytically derived from the traditional GMM used as a conversion model in the conventional SVC.
The traditional GMM is used as a conversion model in the conventional SVC.
Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method makes it possible to significantly improve speech quality in the converted singing voice.
The proposed method preserves the conversion accuracy of singer identity compared to the conventional SVC.
The differential spectral feature is directly estimated.
entities: statistical singing voice conversion ( SVC ) technique
